Key candidates for leaf spots: Early_Blight, Septoria_Leaf_Blotch, Bacterial_Speck_Of_Tomato, Tomato_Spotted_Wilt_Virus, Late_Blight, Leaf_Mold.

TSWV shows ring/mosaic patterns - doesn't match. Checking Late Blight.
Late Blight shows large necrotic patches - doesn't match. Checking Bacterial Speck.
Bacterial Speck looks similar - dark spots on green leaf. Checking Leaf Mold.
Leaf Mold shows pale yellowing - doesn't match. Checking Gray Mold.
Gray Mold shows large necrotic areas - doesn't match. Checking Powdery Mildew.

Powdery Mildew shows white coating - doesn't match.

**Summary of comparisons:**
- **Septoria_Leaf_Blotch**: Circular dark spots on green leaf - very similar pattern to test image
- **Bacterial_Speck_Of_Tomato**: Small dark spots - similar but spots seem smaller/uniform
- Early_Blight, Late_Blight, Gray_Mold, TSWV, Leaf_Mold, Powdery_Mildew: all clearly different

The test image shows multiple discrete circular dark brown/black spots scattered on a green tomato leaf with no yellowing halos, no powdery coating, no large necrotic patches. The Septoria Leaf Blotch reference (CDDM_1928) most closely matches: similar circular spots with darker centers (pycnidia), similar distribution pattern, similar size relative to leaf.
